name: Lev D. Landau
summary: Soviet physicist known for contributions to quantum mechanics, condensed matter, and astrophysics.

name: Niels Bohr
summary: Danish physicist who made foundational contributions to understanding atomic structure and quantum theory.

name: Léon Rosenfeld
summary: Belgian-Danish physicist and collaborator of Niels Bohr.

name: James Chadwick
summary: British physicist who discovered the neutron in 1932.

name: Walter Baade
summary: German astronomer who worked in the US and contributed to stellar evolution theory.

name: Fritz Zwicky
summary: Swiss physicist and astronomer who proposed the existence of neutron stars.

name: Yakov I. Frenkel
summary: Soviet physicist and Landau's supervisor at Leningrad Physical Technical Institute.

name: Matvei P. Bronstein
summary: Soviet theoretical physicist and colleague of Landau.

name: P. L. Kapitsa
summary: Soviet physicist who defended Landau during his arrest.

name: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar
summary: Astrophysicist known for the Chandrasekhar limit of white dwarf mass.

name: Dmitry Ivanenko
summary: Soviet physicist who proposed the proton-neutron model of atomic nuclei.

name: Joseph Stalin
summary: Leader of the Soviet Union during Landau's arrest.

name: Leningrad State University
summary: University where Landau graduated in 1927.

name: Leningrad Physical Technical Institute
summary: Research institute where Landau was appointed after graduation.

name: Institute for Theoretical Physics
summary: Institute in Copenhagen where Bohr worked and Landau visited.

name: Copenhagen
summary: City in Denmark where Bohr's institute was located.

name: Zurich
summary: City in Switzerland where Landau wrote his 1931 paper.

name: Kharkov
summary: City in Ukraine where Landau moved after returning from abroad.

name: Moscow
summary: Capital of the USSR where Landau was arrested.

name: On the theory of stars
summary: Paper by Landau predicting dense stars and calculating white dwarf mass.

name: Nature
summary: Scientific journal where Chadwick's discovery and pulsar discovery were published.

name: Physikalische Zeitschrift der Sowjetunion
summary: Soviet physical journal where Landau's 1932 paper was published.
